mainTopic: Conduct while bathing, רב יהודה's bathhouse lessons, and heating water in hot vessels on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer about רבי אבהו swimming: the ban applies to a pool without raised banks, and רבי אבהו swam in one that had banks. רבי זירא then reports that רבי אבהו covered himself with his hands while bathing. אביי explains that the fear of the river keeps a bather from improper thoughts, just as fear of war keeps soldiers from pouring wine for idols. The גמרא resolves רב's warning that covering oneself looks like denying ברית אברהם: covering is forbidden going into the river and allowed coming out, in front of people. Next comes the story of רבי זירא, who wanted to move to ארץ ישראל and first heard רב יהודה give his servant instructions in the bathhouse. The גמרא explains each instruction, and a ברייתא of health advice explains why one should drink the bathhouse water. A new משנה then permits drinking on שבת from a swept מוליאר but not from an אנטיכי, and a ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק that an אנטיכי is a copper cauldron. Finally, a משנה about an emptied hot urn is explained by רב אדא בר מתנא: a small amount of water is forbidden because it would get hot, and a large amount is permitted because it would only get lukewarm.

steps.title: Finishing the answer: a pool without embankments versus a pool with embankments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes an answer that began on the previous amud. The source that forbids swimming is about a pool with no raised banks. רבי אבהו's case was a pool that does have banks.
steps.simpleTranslation: [This source that forbids it is about a pool] that has no embankments. That [case of רבי אבהו] is about one that has embankments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a 'this case versus that case' answer that began on the previous amud. It explains why רבי אבהו was allowed to swim there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pool without banks looks like an open river or sea, so the rabbis forbade swimming in it. A pool with banks looks like a container, so the rabbis did not forbid it. This removes the contradiction between רבי אבהו's conduct and the source that forbids swimming.

keyTerms.meaning: Embankments or raised banks around a pool

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The word הָא ('this case') that opens the answer is at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: [this is a pool] that does not have embankments,
phrases.notes: Without banks it looks like a river or sea, so swimming there is forbidden.

phrases.english: that [case] is one that has embankments.
phrases.notes: With banks it looks like a container, so swimming there is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to a question raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (אוקימתא of two cases)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source forbidding swimming seemed to contradict רבי אבהו's conduct.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition applies only to a pool without banks. רבי אבהו swam in a pool with banks.

steps.title: רבי זירא's report: רבי אבהו covered himself while bathing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that he saw רבי אבהו put his hands over his private parts while bathing. He did not know whether רבי אבהו actually touched them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: I saw רבי אבהו place his hands over his lower area [his private parts], and I do not know whether he touched or did not touch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report from רבי זירא about how רבי אבהו behaved while bathing. רבי זירא says he is unsure about one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering oneself for modesty is one thing. Actually touching is a more serious question. רבי זירא leaves it open whether רבי אבהו touched, and that open question sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His 'lower face', a polite way to say his private parts

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
I saw Rabbi Abbahu

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִנִּיחַ יָדָיו כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל מַטָּה,
phrases.english: that he placed his hands over his private parts,
phrases.notes: He did this for modesty while bathing.

phrases.english: and I do not know
whether he touched or did not touch.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֲנָא חֲזִיתֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new report from the same speaker about the same רבי אבהו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו covered himself while bathing. It is unclear whether he touched himself.

steps.title: Why the doubt? Touching is obviously forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's doubt. It must be obvious that רבי אבהו did not touch, because רבי אליעזר teaches that holding oneself is like bringing a flood on the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that he did not touch! As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, anyone who holds his organ while urinating is as if he brings a flood to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רבי זירא was unsure at all. It brings a ברייתא showing that touching is extremely severe, so a great rabbi like רבי אבהו surely would not do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats touching as very dangerous because it can lead to improper thoughts and wasting seed. That sin is compared to the sins of the generation of the מבול. If touching is that serious, רבי זירא should have had no doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the ברייתא is a source, it is not here to prove a new law. Its job is to attack רבי זירא's doubt, so this step works as a challenge.

phrases.english: It is obvious that he did not touch,
as it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
anyone who holds his organ and urinates —
it is as if he brings a flood to the world.
phrases.notes: Touching can lead to arousal, which is compared to the sins of the generation of the מבול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt raised in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's uncertainty about whether רבי אבהו touched himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Touching is a severe sin according to רבי אליעזר, so there should be no room for doubt.

steps.title: אביי: the rabbis treated it like a military troop
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the case may be like a בולשת, a troop of soldiers. Different conditions can change the usual concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They made it like a military troop.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a short answer to defend רבי זירא's doubt. He is setting up a comparison that the next step will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי suggests that the usual worry about touching may not apply in this situation. He compares it to a known law about a בולשת. The details of that comparison are given right after.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it [equal to], they treated it like
A military troop that searches through a city

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They made it like a military troop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Touching should be forbidden in every situation, so there is no room for doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Special circumstances, such as fear, can remove the concern. So it is possible רבי אבהו touched.

steps.title: The משנה of the troop: frightened people do not sin
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the משנה. In peacetime, open wine barrels left after a troop of non-Jewish soldiers are forbidden. In wartime, all barrels are permitted, because frightened soldiers have no time to pour wine for idol worship. In the same way, a frightened bather will not come to improper thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a troop that entered a city in peacetime, open barrels are forbidden and sealed ones are permitted. In wartime, both are permitted, because there is no free time to pour libations. So we see that since they are afraid, they do not pour libations. Here too, since he is afraid, he will not come to improper thoughts.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the source for his comparison and applies it to the bather. The basic idea is that fear stops a person from sinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In peacetime we worry the soldiers poured the wine for idol worship (יין נסך). In wartime they are too afraid and busy, so we are not concerned. אביי takes that logic and says a frightened bather is too busy to have improper thoughts, so touching would not be as dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
To pour wine as an offering to idols

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea of the rabbis: a person who is afraid or busy is not suspected of a sin that needs calm and attention.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
a military troop that entered a city,
in a time of peace —
open barrels are forbidden,
phrases.notes: The soldiers may have poured from them for idol worship.

phrases.english: sealed ones are permitted.
in a time of war —
both these and those are permitted,
because there is no free time to pour libations.
We see that since they are frightened
they do not pour libations.
Here too, since he is frightened
he will not come to improper thoughts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning behind אביי's comparison in step 4
steps.raayaObject: The idea that fear removes the concern of improper thoughts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a בולשת in wartime

steps.title: What is there to be afraid of here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what fear a person who is bathing has, which would be like the fear of war.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what fear is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about אביי's comparison. It wants to know what the bather is afraid of, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers' fear of war is obvious. A bather does not seem to be in danger. So the comparison needs a real source of fear before it can work.

phrases.english: Here, what fear is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail of the comparison in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What fear exists for someone who is bathing

steps.title: Fear of the river
steps.stepSummary: The fear is of the river itself. The bather is careful not to be swept away by the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fear of the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bather is afraid of the river's current. That fear keeps his mind busy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being careful not to be carried off by the water keeps the bather focused. A focused mind does not drift into improper thoughts. So אביי's comparison works, and it is possible רבי אבהו touched without any problem.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי זירא's doubt made sense. Fear of the river keeps a bather from improper thoughts, just as fear of war keeps soldiers from pouring wine for idols.

phrases.english: Fear of the river.
phrases.notes: He must take care that the current does not sweep him away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fear is of the river's current.

steps.title: Covering oneself looks like denying ברית אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the whole story. רב said that anyone who covers his private parts with his hands is like someone who denies the ברית מילה of אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב: anyone who places his hands over his private parts is as if he denies the covenant of אברהם אבינו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the basic fact that רבי אבהו covered himself at all. It quotes רב, who says that covering oneself is a very bad thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the ברית מילה looks as if one is embarrassed by it or hiding it. So the problem now is not touching at all. The problem is the act of covering itself, which רבי אבהו did.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (an opening that signals a challenge)
The covenant of אברהם אבינו, the ברית מילה

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּנִּיחַ יָדָיו כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל מַטָּה
phrases.english: anyone who places his hands over his private parts

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ כּוֹפֵר בִּבְרִיתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ!
phrases.english: is as if he denies the covenant of Abraham our father!
phrases.notes: It looks as if he is hiding that he is circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the report of step 2 and challenges the covering itself
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's act of placing his hands over his private parts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says covering oneself is like denying the ברית, so how could רבי אבהו do it?

steps.title: Going in versus coming out of the river
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two different cases. Covering is forbidden when going down into the river and is allowed when coming up out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is when he goes down, and that is when he comes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction between רב and רבי אבהו's behavior by splitting the cases by direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When going into the water, no people are facing him, so there is no modesty reason to cover. Then covering only looks like hiding the ברית, and that is forbidden. When coming out, he faces the people on the bank, so covering for modesty is allowed, and that is what רבי אבהו did.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: רב's rule is not cancelled here. It still applies when going into the water. Coming out is an exception, because modesty is needed in front of the people on the bank.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is when he goes down,
phrases.notes: Here covering is forbidden, because no one is facing him.

phrases.english: that is when he comes up.
phrases.notes: Here covering is allowed for modesty, because people are facing him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא כִּי נָחֵית, הָא כִּי סָלֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (going down versus coming up)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering oneself is always forbidden because of רב's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Covering is forbidden when going in. It is allowed when coming out, for the sake of modesty.

steps.title: How the sages actually behaved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes what the sages did. רבא would bend over, רבי זירא would stand straight, and the רבנן of רב אשי's school stood straight going in and bent over coming out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this: רבא would bend over. רבי זירא would stand straight. The רבנן of the house of רב אשי, when going down, would stand straight, and when coming up, would bend over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the distinction with the real practice of the sages. Some covered themselves by bending over, some stood straight, and one group did each at the right time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bending over is a way of covering for modesty. Standing straight avoids looking like one is hiding the ברית. The רבנן of רב אשי's school did both, matching exactly the split of going in versus coming out.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of the school of רב אשי

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: covering oneself is like denying ברית אברהם when there is no modesty reason, such as when going into the river. When coming out in front of people, covering by bending over is proper. The school of רב אשי followed both rules.

phrases.english: Like this: Rava would bend over.
phrases.notes: He covered himself for modesty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira would stand upright.
phrases.notes: This follows רב's concern about the ברית.

phrases.english: The Sages of the school of Rav Ashi,
when they went down — they stood upright,
when they came up — they bent over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction of step 9 with the actual practice of the sages
steps.raayaObject: The split between going into and coming out of the river
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practices of רבא, רבי זירא, and the רבנן of רב אשי's school
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Stand straight when going in. Bend over for modesty when coming out.

steps.title: רבי זירא avoids his teacher because he wants to move to ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא avoided רב יהודה because he wanted to go up to ארץ ישראל, and רב יהודה held that going up from בבל violates a positive commandment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא was avoiding רב יהודה, because he wanted to go up to ארץ ישראל. רב יהודה said: Anyone who goes up from בבל to ארץ ישראל transgresses a positive commandment, as the verse says: 'They will be brought to Babylon, and there they will stay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story connected to the bathhouse theme. First it sets the background: רבי זירא wanted to move, and his teacher held that moving was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads the verse in ירמיהו as a command. The Jews of the exile must stay in בבל until God brings them back. So רבי זירא did not want to face his teacher and openly go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: they will be brought to Babylon and there they will stay (ירמיהו כ״ז)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira was avoiding Rav Yehuda,
because he wanted to go up to the Land of Israel.
For Rav Yehuda said:
Anyone who goes up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel
transgresses a positive commandment,
as it says: 'They will be brought to Babylon and there they will stay.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו כ״ז:כ״ב

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the bathing theme of steps 2-10 with a new story, this time set in a bathhouse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יהודה, leaving בבל for ארץ ישראל violates a positive commandment, based on ירמיהו.

steps.title: רבי זירא hears רב יהודה's bathhouse instructions
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא went to hear one last teaching. He found רב יהודה in the bathhouse giving instructions to his servant, and said that hearing this alone was worth the trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I will go and hear something from him, and then I will go up. He went and found רב יהודה standing in the bathhouse, telling his servant: Bring me natron, bring me a comb, open your mouths and let out the steam, and drink from the bathhouse water. רבי זירא said: Even if I had come only to hear this, it would be enough for me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא goes to learn one final lesson before leaving. What he hears is simple-sounding bathhouse instructions, and he says they were worth the trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The instructions look ordinary, but רבי זירא sees Torah lessons in them. That sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains what each instruction teaches.

phrases.english: He said: I will go and hear something from him
and then I will come and go up.
He went and found him standing in the bathhouse
and saying to his servant:

phrases.aramaic: הָבִיאוּ לִי נֶתֶר, הָבִיאוּ לִי מַסְרֵק,
phrases.english: Bring me natron, bring me a comb,
open your mouths and let out the steam,
and drink from the water of the bathhouse.
He said: Even if I had come
only to hear this thing, it would be enough for me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's bathhouse instructions: natron, a comb, letting out steam, and drinking the bathhouse water.

steps.title: What is the benefit of drinking the bathhouse water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first instructions: speaking ordinary matters in לשון קודש in a bathhouse is allowed, and steam brings out more sweat. Then it asks what benefit there is in drinking the bathhouse water.
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand 'bring natron, bring a comb.' This teaches that ordinary matters may be said in לשון קודש in the bathhouse. We also understand 'open your mouths and let out the steam,' which follows שמואל, who said: Heat brings out heat. But 'drink the bathhouse water,' what is the benefit of that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through רב יהודה's instructions one by one. It is comfortable with the first two, but asks about the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא' format means: 'These parts make sense, but this one does not.' The first instruction teaches a הלכה, and the second matches שמואל's statement about heat. The drinking instruction has no clear source yet, so the גמרא asks what it is good for.
steps.confusionAlert: Holy words may not be spoken in a bathhouse. The lesson here is the opposite case: ordinary requests like 'bring me a comb' may be said there even in לשון קודש, the holy language.

phrases.english: Granted, 'bring natron, bring a comb' —
teaches us that ordinary matters
may be said in the holy language.
'Open your mouths and let out the steam' —
also follows Shmuel,
for Shmuel said: Heat brings out heat.
But 'drink the bathhouse water' —
what is the benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the instructions quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What benefit comes from drinking the hot bathhouse water?

steps.title: A ברייתא of health advice explains why to drink the bathhouse water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists health rules about eating, drinking, and bathing. One of them says that bathing in hot water without drinking it is like an oven heated only from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: One who ate and did not drink, his food becomes blood, and that is the start of intestinal illness. One who ate and did not walk four אמות, his food rots, and that is the start of bad breath. One who needs the bathroom and eats is like an oven lit on top of its old ashes, and that is the start of body odor. One who bathed in hot water and did not drink from it is like an oven heated from the outside but not from the inside. One who bathed in hot water and did not rinse with cold water is like iron put into fire but not then put into cold water. One who bathed and did not rub on oil is like water poured over the top of a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13 by quoting a ברייתא of health tips. The key line is the one about drinking hot water while bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bathing heats the body from the outside. Drinking the hot water heats it from the inside too, so the body is warmed properly, like an oven heated on both sides. The rest of the ברייתא is quoted because it is one connected list.

keyTerms.meaning: one who needs to relieve himself
the smell of body filth, body odor

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה told his servant to drink the bathhouse water so he would be warmed from the inside as well as the outside, like an oven heated on both sides.

phrases.english: For it was taught: One who ate and did not drink —
his food becomes blood,
and this is the start of intestinal illness.
One who ate and did not walk four cubits —
his food rots,
and this is the start of bad breath.
One who needs to relieve himself and ate —

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹמֶה לְתַנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ עַל גַּבֵּי אֶפְרוֹ,
phrases.english: is like an oven lit on top of its old ashes,
and this is the start of body odor.
One who bathed in hot water and did not drink from it —
is like an oven heated from the outside
and not heated from the inside.
One who bathed in hot water and did not rinse with cold —
is like iron put into the fire
and not then put into cold water.
One who bathed and did not rub on oil —
is like water poured over the top of a barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drinking hot water while bathing heats the body from the inside, as the ברייתא compares to an oven heated both inside and outside.

steps.title: משנה: drinking from a swept מוליאר versus an אנטיכי on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one may drink on שבת from a מוליאר whose coals were swept out, but not from an אנטיכי, even if its coals were swept out.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A מוליאר whose coals were swept out, one may drink from it on שבת. An אנטיכי, even though its coals were swept out, one may not drink from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares two kinds of water-heating vessels and their status on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once its coals are swept, the מוליאר no longer heats the water strongly, so its water is allowed. The אנטיכי keeps so much heat even after sweeping that its water is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a water-heating vessel with a compartment for coals
a different kind of water-heating vessel

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A mulyar that was swept of its coals —
one may drink from it on Shabbat.
An antikhi, even though it was swept —
one may not drink from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מוּלְיָאר הַגָּרוּף שׁוֹתִין הֵימֶנּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the bathhouse story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water from a swept מוליאר is permitted on שבת. Water from an אנטיכי is forbidden even if it was swept.

steps.title: What exactly is a swept מוליאר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of a swept מוליאר looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the case of a swept מוליאר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for a description of the vessel in the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To understand why one vessel is permitted and the other forbidden, we first need to know how each one is built.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case, what does it look like

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the case of
a swept mulyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the first vessel in the משנה of step 15.

steps.title: A מוליאר has water inside and coals outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that a מוליאר holds the water in an inner part and the coals in an outer part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: water on the inside and coals on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a short ברייתא describing how a מוליאר is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the coals sit off to the side and not under the water, sweeping them out removes the main heat source. That is why its water is allowed.

phrases.english: It was taught: water on the inside
and coals on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מוליאר has water in the inner part and coals in the outer part.

steps.title: רבה and רב נחמן בר יצחק disagree about what an אנטיכי is
steps.stepSummary: רבה says an אנטיכי is a stove-like vessel. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is a cauldron-like vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: אנטיכי: רבה said it is a stove. רב נחמן בר יצחק said it is a cauldron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now defines the second vessel. Two אמוראים disagree about what it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the אנטיכי is a stove with a space for water, which holds very strong heat. According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, it is two cauldrons stacked together, with coals underneath and water on top.

phrases.english: An antikhi: Rabba said —
it is a stove.
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said —
it is a cauldron.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the מוליאר to defining the אנטיכי from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה holds an אנטיכי is a stove. רב נחמן בר יצחק holds it is a cauldron.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two views
steps.stepSummary: Whoever forbids the cauldron surely forbids the stove. Whoever forbids only the stove would permit the cauldron.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is a cauldron would certainly forbid a stove. But the one who says it is a stove would not forbid a cauldron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical difference between רבה and רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stove holds more heat than a cauldron. So רב נחמן, who forbids even a cauldron, certainly forbids a stove. רבה forbids only the stronger stove, which leaves a cauldron permitted. The real disagreement is about the cauldron.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב נחמן's view is the stricter one, which matters when the next step brings a ברייתא supporting him.

phrases.english: The one who says a cauldron
all the more so a stove;
and the one who says a stove,
but a cauldron — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּי דוּדֵי כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בֵּי כִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical outcome of the disagreement in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן both are forbidden. According to רבה only a stove is forbidden, and a cauldron is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that an אנטיכי is forbidden even if its coals were swept and covered with ash, because its copper heats the water. This fits רב נחמן's view that it is a metal cauldron.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in support of רב נחמן: An אנטיכי, even if it was swept and covered with ash, one may not drink from it, because its copper heats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's definition of an אנטיכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason 'its copper heats it.' That describes a metal vessel like a cauldron, not a stove. So the ברייתא matches רב נחמן, who defines the אנטיכי as a cauldron.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught that supports him

steps.whatToRemember: A swept מוליאר is permitted on שבת. An אנטיכי is forbidden even if swept and covered with ash, and the ברייתא supports רב נחמן that it is a copper cauldron whose metal keeps the water hot.

phrases.english: It was taught in support of Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: אַנְטִיכֵי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגְּרוּפָה וּקְטוּמָה
phrases.english: An antikhi, even though it was swept and covered with ash,
one may not drink from it,
because its copper heats it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the disagreement from steps 18-19.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's view that an אנטיכי is a cauldron
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that an אנטיכי is forbidden because its copper heats it

steps.title: The משנה on refilling an emptied hot urn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that cold water may not be put into an emptied hot urn to heat it, but may be put into it, or into a cup, to take the chill off.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An urn that was emptied of its hot water: one may not put cold water into it so that the water will get hot. But one may put cold water into it, or into a cup, just to make the water lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what you may and may not do with a hot urn (מֵיחַם) on שבת after its hot water has been poured out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urn is still very hot even after it has been emptied. Putting cold water in so that it becomes truly hot would be like cooking, which is forbidden on שבת. Putting water in only to take the chill off (לְהַפְשִׁיר) is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, the base text the גמרא will discuss
An urn or kettle used to heat water
He emptied it, meaning he poured out its hot water
To make lukewarm, just taking the chill off without making it truly hot

steps.confusionAlert: Read quickly, the משנה seems to say both 'don't put water in' and 'you may put water in.' That is not a mistake. It is exactly the problem the גמרא is about to address.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: An urn that one emptied
phrases.notes: Its hot water was poured out, but the urn itself is still hot.

phrases.english: one may not put cold water into it
so that they become hot.
phrases.notes: Making the water truly hot is the forbidden goal.

phrases.english: But one may put [water] into it
or into the cup
in order to make them lukewarm.
phrases.notes: Only taking the chill off is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from the stove-like and cauldron-like vessels to the case of an emptied hot urn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cold water may not be put into an emptied hot urn so that it heats up. It may be put in to make it lukewarm.

steps.title: What is the משנה really saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means, since it seems to forbid and then permit the same act.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means. This question sets up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the משנה forbids putting water into the urn, and the second half permits putting water into the urn. The question points out that these two halves seem to clash. It asks for a reading that makes them fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
What is it saying? A request to explain the meaning of a text that seems unclear or self-contradictory

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: This marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: The משנה seems to contradict itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה in step 21, which appears to contradict itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the משנה both forbid and permit putting water into the emptied urn?

steps.title: The difference is the amount of water
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא explains that a small amount of water is forbidden because it would get hot. A large amount is permitted because it would only become lukewarm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said: This is what it means. An urn that was emptied of its hot water: one may not put a small amount of water into it so that it gets hot. But one may put a large amount of water into it to make it lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנא answers the question. The two halves of the משנה are talking about different amounts of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A little water in a hot urn would become truly hot, which counts as cooking, so it is forbidden. A lot of water cannot get that hot from the urn's leftover heat. It only gets lukewarm, so it is allowed. Now the משנה has no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. The formula used to introduce a clarifying reading

steps.whatToRemember: An emptied hot urn: a small amount of water is forbidden because it will get hot, which is cooking. A large amount of water is permitted because it will only get lukewarm.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling depends on what will actually happen to the water. If it will truly heat up, it is forbidden. If it will only warm slightly, it is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said,
this is what it is saying:
An urn from which one emptied hot water
one may not put a small amount of water into it
so that it will get hot,
phrases.notes: A little water would truly heat up.

phrases.english: but one may put a large amount of water into it
in order to make it lukewarm.
phrases.notes: A lot of water only gets lukewarm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22 by reading the משנה as two different cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first half of the משנה is about a small amount of water, which would get hot and is forbidden. The second half is about a large amount of water, which would only become lukewarm and is permitted.
